title: Guarding against prompt injection and sanitising user text

videos.script: A customer message is data. The trouble is that the model reads it in the same stream as your instructions. A sentence inside it can look exactly like an order. {{stream}} Prompt engineering introduced this as injection. This lesson asks a narrower question: how much does each defence actually stop? {{title}} You start with ten messages the course wrote for the purpose. Each carries a small instruction, harmless on purpose. With nothing to mark where the message ends, the stand-in obeys every one it recognises. {{undelimited}} Then you add defences one at a time. Tags around the message, and a sentence saying it is data. Escaping, so the message cannot close its own tag. A strict check on what comes back. {{layers}} Each layer cuts the count, and none of them takes it to zero. {{counts}} You try a scanner that looks for suspicious phrases. It flags an honest customer and misses two of the instructions. {{scan}} Last, you plant a meaningless string in the prompt, and a check finds the one reply that repeated it. {{canary}} By the end you can say which defence stopped what, with a number beside each one. {{close}}
